head:
]Executive Orber.
Mr. Guy Emerson may be appointed a Special Agent of the Treasury
Department without compliance with Civil Service Rules.
This Order is issued for the reason that Mr. Emerson, who is Private
Secretary to Assistant Secretary Curtis, has been brought into close touch
with the practical administration of customs affairs through his service as
Chairman of the Customs Committee, and as a member of the Commission
on the Reorganizati on of Appraising Methods in the Customs Service.
He has also been assigned to numerous special missions for the Secretary
and Assistant Secretary, and his work in these special directions has reached
such a magnitude that it has exceeded in importance his duties as Private
Secretary, and has made it expedient to have him so situated that he can
devote all of his time to administrative questions that fall within the juris-
diction of the Special Agents' force.
Mr. Emerson is a graduate of law and is unusually well equipped men-
tally for the discharge of the duties which will fall to him as a Special
Agent.
It is the desire of the Secretary of the Treasury that, as a Special
Agent, Mr. Emerson shall be able to continue uninterruptedly the various
investigations relating to remedial and constructive measures for the benefit
of customs administration. For the reasons stated the Civil Service Coin-
mission approves this order.
WM H TAFT
THE WVHITrE HOUSE,
Oct Ober 28, 1912.
[No. 1635.]

AMENDMENT TO THE CIVIL SERVICE RULES.
Schedule A of classified positions excepted from examination under
Rule II, clause 3, is hereby amended by adding to Subdivision VIII,
Department of the Interior, the following paragraph:
26. All employees of the Neopit Lumber Mills on the
Menominee Indian reservation in Wisconsin.
The Neopit Lumbering Project is a commercial enterprise conducted
for the profit and sole benefit of the Menominee tribe of Indians, and in
its operation is in competition with private enterprises of the same kind.
It thus differs from any other enterprise conducted for the benefit of the
Indians, and as it was believed by the Secretary of the Interior that the
work could be carried on more economically and therefore with more
benefit to the Indians with freedom of employment he recommended that
the employees be excepted from examination. After full and careful
consideration, the Civil Service Commission reached the conclusion that
the conditions surrounding the operation of the Neopit Lumber Mills
warrant it in concurring in the recommendation of the Secretary of the
Interior.

the Department of the Navy, are hereby included in the competitive
classified service of the United States, unless specifically exempted from
examination by law or Executive order. Such positions will hereafter be
filled in accordance with the regulations which have been approved by me,
except that employment from the present registered lists, without classifi-
cation, is authorized for the limited period necessary to establish eligible
lists through open competitive examination in the manner provided in the
regulations.

classified service by this order shall be classified unless he has established
his capacity for efficient service or has been examined and found qualified
by the Labor Board and is recommended for classification by the Com-

head:
Executive eter
Mr. George J. Bunce mayr be reinstated in a subclerical position in the
Mint and Assay Service of the United States without reference to the
period of his separation from the service.
Mr. Bunce was an employee of the United States Assay Office at
New York for nearly forty years and was for most of the time one of the
most trusted melters. Ill health required his separation from the service
on January 16, 1911. It was desired to treat his separation as a furlough,
which would have rendered him eligible for reemployment within three
years, but such action was not in accordance with the regulations. He
has now recovered his health sufficiently to be able to perform light work,
serve as doorman or upon the day watch, and is in needy circumstances.
During his employment he handled hundreds of millions of dollars worth
of precious metals and was a competent, faithful and valued employee.
This order is requested by the Director of the Mint and recommended
by the Secretary of the Treasury in recognition of Mr. Bunce's long and
faithful service to the Government in a position of trust and responsibility,
and the Civil Service Commission concurs.
WM H TAFT
THE WHITE HOUSE,
January 24, 1913.
[No. 1687.]
